children: SOAR AI, Inc. (NYSE American: SOAR), formerly known as Volato Group, Inc. (“SOAR AI” or the “Company”), today provided a construction update on its AI compute campus in Chillicothe, Ohio. Low-voltage data hall transformers and cooling plant equipment are being installed this week, and the Company remains on schedule to place its first 4,096 AMD Instinct™ MI355X GPUs in service on December 31, 2026, with customer revenue expected to begin in January 2027.

The data hall, at a former paper mill, is being converted into an AI facility with closed-loop liquid cooling. Following the MI355X deployment, the Company intends to deploy 4,032 next-generation AMD Instinct™ MI455X GPUs on the AMD Helios™ rack-scale platform, with the data hall expected to be ready to accept them in February 2027 and a contractual in-service date of June 30, 2027. The campus has 154 megawatts of power available today and a roadmap to 480 megawatts.

The GPU deployment is supported by a master services agreement and two four-year, take-or-pay orders representing $1.17 billion in aggregate contract value. The MI355X GPUs and the first 4,032 MI455X GPUs are planned to fulfill these orders, giving the Company long-term revenue visibility. Revenue under the first order is expected to begin in January 2027, subject to delivery and acceptance. Based on the contracted rates and anticipated service start dates, the Company expects these orders to generate revenue of approximately $175 million to $200 million in 2027.
Installation of the data hall's power and cooling equipment is under way:
The substation, medium-voltage distribution and turbine backup power systems are active and commissioned.
Low-voltage data hall transformers are being installed this week.
Cooling plant equipment is on site and being installed now.
Piping, wiring and other materials for the data hall have arrived on schedule.
4,096 AMD Instinct™ MI355X GPUs in service
Data hall ready to accept 4,032 AMD Instinct™ MI455X GPUs on AMD Helios™
Up to two additional tranches of 4,032 MI455X GPUs each, for future customers
Second half of 2027, subject to financing and customer contracts

The facility uses direct liquid cooling at the rack, with heat rejected through the mill’s existing water system for year-round free cooling. The design targets a power usage effectiveness (PUE) of approximately 1.08. The data hall is designed to Uptime Institute Tier III concurrent maintainability standards.

The campus repurposes a paper mill that closed in 2025, reusing its power and water infrastructure. The project returns an idle industrial site to productive use, bringing skilled construction and technical work to the Chillicothe area while limiting the need for new utility infrastructure.

The Company plans up to two additional tranches of 4,032 MI455X GPUs each for future customers, targeted to enter service in the second half of 2027, which together with the contracted deployment would bring the campus to as many as 16,192 GPUs. These tranches are subject to securing financing and customer contracts, and could be accelerated if both come together sooner. The Company is also actively exploring additional data center sites in the United States and internationally.

“Less than two months after closing our merger, we are turning a shuttered Ohio paper mill into one of the most advanced AI compute facilities in the Midwest,” said Chris Ensey, Chief Executive Officer of SOAR AI. “Reusing the mill’s existing power and water infrastructure, combined with direct liquid cooling, lets us bring capacity online in months rather than years. Our power systems are commissioned, and the data hall equipment is going in now. We expect our first AMD Instinct MI355X GPUs to be serving our first customer on December 31, with next-generation MI455X GPUs on the Helios platform to follow in 2027.”

“This deployment is the first step in converting our power and site advantages into contracted, recurring revenue,” said Mark Heinen, Chief Financial Officer of SOAR AI. “We remain focused on disciplined execution and on funding the build-out efficiently as we move toward first revenue in January 2027.”

SOAR AI, Inc. (NYSE American: SOAR), formerly known as Volato Group, Inc., is an AI infrastructure and software company focused on the development and operation of AI infrastructure and AI-powered software solutions. The Company is constructing an AI infrastructure campus in Ohio that combines data center infrastructure, high-density GPU compute, high-performance networking and related technology to support AI, machine learning and high-performance computing workloads. The Company also develops AI-powered operational systems for aviation businesses through its Aviation AI platform and operates Vaunt, a technology-enabled private aviation membership platform. The name SOAR, Sovereign AI Resources, reflects the Company’s strategy of developing AI infrastructure that gives customers greater control over their data, models and computing environments.
